issues.detail: The Greek 'τω θεω' (to God) is the object of 'χαριν εχω' (I give thanks). The Vietnamese 'Đấng tôi phục vụ' (Whom I serve) incorrectly attributes the action of 'serving' to the subject, whereas the Greek 'λατρευω' is an infinitive describing the manner/reason for the thanks. Furthermore, 'απο προγονων' (from my ancestors) is rendered as 'như tổ phụ tôi' (like my ancestors), changing a source/origin into a comparison.

The Greek 'εχω την περι σου μνειαν' (I have the remembrance of You) refers to God ('σου'). The Vietnamese 'nhắc đến con' (remind/mention me) incorrectly changes the object of remembrance from God to the self.
